name.text: Relations Q4 - Admission numbers at Green Valley Secondary School

questiontext.text:
[[if test="is(ctx=1)"]]

At Green Valley Secondary School in Nakuru, every new Form One student is given exactly one admission number, and no two students ever share the same admission number. Part of the pairing is shown below.

  • Amina is paired with GV101.
  • Brian is paired with GV102.
  • Cynthia is paired with GV103.
  • David is paired with GV104.

Treating the students as the domain and the admission numbers as the codomain, what type of relation does this pairing represent?

[[else]]

In Kenya, every citizen who registers for a national identity card is issued exactly one ID number, and that ID number is never given to any other person.

Treating the citizens as the domain and the ID numbers as the codomain, what type of relation does this pairing represent?

[[/if]]
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
To classify a relation, check both directions: how many outputs each input has, and how many inputs share each output.

[[if test="is(ctx=1)"]]

Each student has exactly one admission number, so no input has more than one output. Each admission number belongs to exactly one student, so no output is shared by two inputs.

[[else]]

Each citizen receives exactly one ID number, so no input has more than one output. No ID number is reused for a different citizen, so no output is shared by two inputs.

[[/if]]

Every element of the domain maps to exactly one element of the codomain, and every output traces back to only one input. The relation is one-to-one. The correct answer is C.

One-to-one pairings like this matter in practice because they can be reversed without any conflict: given a number, you can find the one person who holds it.

questionnote.text: ctx={@ctx@} (1 admission numbers, 2 national ID); key C (one-to-one).

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the definitions of one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations in Section 16.1 (Types of Relations) of the Grade 11 Functions topic. It merges the former Relations Q9 (national ID numbers) into this question as a second context.

falsefeedback.text: Check both directions. Can one person be linked to more than one number? Can one number be linked to more than one person? Use the two answers to name the relation type.
